# Synthetic MacroFactor regression fixtures

These files were authored for Ripper OS on 2026-09-05. **They are synthetic test
data, not anonymized real MacroFactor exports.** They contain no person's training
history or identifiers. Their schema models the fields currently consumed by
`lib/training-parser.ts`; they do not establish support for unverified export
variants. No source application version or export locale is claimed.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `six-months.csv` | Readable set-oriented input: 384 rows over 24 dates, six exercises, January–June 2026. |
| `workbook-matrix.json` | Authoritative readable cell matrices for all seven supported exercise sheets and the dated muscle-set ledger. |
| `six-months.xlsx` | Full workbook generated from the matrices, with genuine spreadsheet date cells. |
| `optional-sheets-omitted.xlsx` | Same dates with only total sets, total reps and heaviest weight; no muscle, volume, best-rep, e1RM or duration sheet. |
| `build-workbooks.mjs` | Deterministic generator for the two checked-in workbooks. |

Regenerate from the repository root:

```sh
node tests/fixtures/macrofactor/build-workbooks.mjs
npm run test:parser
```

The parser test compares generated bytes with both checked-in workbooks and
generates twice to detect unintended timestamps or randomness. Fixed document
properties and explicit UTC date construction keep these files repeatable.
There is no clock, random seed, external download or personal-file input.

## Coverage and authored conventions

- Calendar coverage is 2026-01-05 through 2026-06-15, spanning six months. March
  intentionally has no training; there is a long February-to-April gap. January
  and June are partial boundary months.
- Each date has three sets apiece of bench press, pull-up, bench dip, back squat
  and lateral raise, plus one timed jump-rope entry: 16 rows per date. Identical
  repeated sets are intentional and must not be deduplicated.
- Bench load rises from 60 kg to a peak of 85 kg on June 1, then ends at 75 kg.
  This allows later tests to distinguish first, latest and peak performance.
- `Wide Grip Pull Up`, `Bench Dips` and `Jumping Rope` exercise the current
  parser's three aliases. Source spellings remain visible in both inputs.
- CSV dates are explicit ISO calendar dates. All weights are explicitly kg,
  durations are seconds, and the synthetic workbook's numeric load/volume/e1RM
  fields are authored in kg-based units. No unit is inferred from a real export.
- CSV rope rows have duration with blank load/reps; bodyweight rows have supplied
  zero external load. Null workbook cells mean absent measurements. The current
  parser may conflate some of these values; these fixtures do not endorse that
  behavior or require it in the future canonical model.
- Workbook e1RM values are **authored source-reported test values**, chosen as
  1.25 times that day's external load for weighted exercises. This is not a
  claim about MacroFactor's formula and must not become an analytics oracle.
- Muscle cells are authored exposure values: chest 4.5, back 3, triceps 4.5,
  quads 3 and shoulders 4.5 per date. They do not specify a physiological model
  or ask Ripper to derive muscle coefficients from these exercises.
- CSV workout IDs/titles/set types and the quoted note `Synthetic fixture, no
  personal data` exercise ignored-column handling. Workout Duration contains
  an authored 2700-second (45-minute) value to exercise the current fallback.
  This is a fixture convention, not a verified source-unit contract.
- The workbook contains daily aggregates only. It cannot establish session
  counts, set pairing or exact CSV/workbook equivalence for every metric.

V2-001 checks fixture reproducibility, coverage and parser acceptance. V2-002
will add independently checked expected analytics. Keep malformed inputs in
separate fixtures/tests; do not corrupt these valid baselines to add error cases.
Future real-export fixtures must have explicit permission and provenance and
must be clearly distinguished from this synthetic family.
